articles.title: Singer Becky Hill looks back: ‘Aside from the music I was making, I hated every minute of my 20s’
articles.summary: The Brit award winner on being scammed by a model agency, coming to terms with sexual assault, and wrestling with impostor syndrome. Born in Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, in 1994 and raised in Bewdley, Becky Hill is a singer and songwriter.
body: This was taken for a kid s’ modelling agency, which we later discovered was a scam. Every stage of the process – getting pictures taken, sending them to the agency, getting them back – cost us more money. We’d wire over £100 and get nothing in return. Our family wasn’t rich, so Mum didn’t tell Dad what we were up to – he probably doesn’t even know about it to this day. As for my modelling ambitions, I never pursued it further. I was cute until the age of seven, then started to go on the turn.

I was a happy, chatty child, but my home life was quite dysfunctional. My parents were on their second marriages, I was their first baby together, and they had five children between the two of them – some lived with us, some didn’t. There was a lot of moving about – a lot of arguing, too, but I always, always felt loved. Everyone had their own taste in music: Mum listened to cassette tapes of Foreigner, Eric Clapton and the Eagles; my sister gave me her computer full of all her downloaded music; and my brother liked Eminem, Blink-182, Slipknot and drum’n’bass.
points: The Brit award winner on being scammed by a model agency, coming to terms with sexual assault, and wrestling with impostor syndrome.

articles.title: My mum has died - and every decision I make about her belongings feels wrong | Polly Hudson
articles.summary: Until now I’d never realised how much work is involved in sorting out a parent’s affairs, and how much heartbreak. In all the talk of the five stages of grief, I don’t recall one of them being spending hours on hold to energy suppliers.
body: You hear the term “sadmin” bandied about, you understand there’s paperwork to do after somebody dies – but until it’s you who has to do it, you don’t realise how much, what it entails or how encompassing it is. My mum’s death has basically become my full-time job. The hours are terrible, the pay is worse and the promotion prospects sobering, to say the least.

Received wisdom is that you should ask your parents lots of questions while they’re still around. For me, this feels increasingly true. There’s so much I now wish I’d asked my mum – namely who her mobile phone provider was and the number of her milkman. I don’t know where the water meter in my own house is, let alone anyone else’s, so it would have been handy if that had come up, too.

I’m lucky my mother died after the introduction of Tell Us Once, the one-stop shop for notifying government departments and council services. But so far my experience is: tell them once, tell everyone else 47 times and prepare yourself for a variety of responses in reaction to the news.
points: Until now I’d never realised how much work is involved in sorting out a parent’s affairs, and how much heartbreak.
In all the talk of the five stages of grief, I don’t recall one of them being spending hours on hold to energy suppliers.

articles.title: How to make the perfect apfelschmarrn – recipe | Felicity Cloake's how to cook the perfect …
articles.summary: This fruity central European pancake dish can be served as part of a main course or as a dessert. Our resident perfektionistin flips through a selection of the best recipes. Schmarr n, or schmarren, Anja Dunk writes, is “peasant food at its best: filling, simple and comforting”.
body: Austro-Hungarian in origin, it’s eaten in both Germany and Austria, and there are many variations, including kaiserschmarren (studded with rum-soaked raisins), savoury potato schmarren, semolina schmarren and bread schmarren, though fruit, often apples, but also stone fruit or berries, seems to be the most common pairing. Whether you’re serving this as a main course (it goes very well with sausages) or afterwards, it’s a very handy addition to the repertoire, especially when paired with soured cream or ice-cream.

articles.title: Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton Have Found Their Loved-up Couple Style Rhythm
articles.summary: From Lake Como to London, the couple quickly found their style sensibilities overlap often. An appearance at the Lucas Museum proved it’s red carpet-worthy.
body: Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton have been taking their romance across the globe: from boating on Lake Como to riding Lime Bikes in London and witnessing history at Celine Dion’s Paris residency show. Their latest appearance, at the Lucas Museum Of Narrative Art’s opening night in Los Angeles, marked a major moment for the loved-up couple.

Having just returned from London where she was celebrating her Skims flagship store opening, Kardashian zipped back across the pond to support her F1 driver boyfriend as he served as an evening co-chair for the grand opening celebration. She opted for a shimmering black and floral embroidered Saint Laurent by Tom Ford fall 2004 dress with a mint underlining, paired with Oscar Heyman earrings and a Zydo ring. It was a look that hit all the Kim Kardashian style pressure points: sparkly, skin-tight, super glam.
Makeup and hair followed a similar beat, with her hair slicked back into a bun, chiseled and warm contour, and siren-like eyes.
points: From Lake Como to London, the couple quickly found their style sensibilities overlap often.
An appearance at the Lucas Museum proved it’s red carpet-worthy.

articles.title: From the Archives: Inside Stefano Gabbana and Domenico Dolce’s Glamorous Milan Apartment
articles.summary: In a Milan triplex, Stefano Gabbana and Domenico Dolce have created an environment as glamorous—and leopard-laden—as their fashion. Hamish Bowles drops in on their dolce vita.
body: “Animal Magnetism,” by Hamish Bowles, was originally published in the May 2000 issue of Vogue.
As their glamorous new Milanese penthouse bears witness, designers Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana are as much mix-masters at home as they are on the runways.

IN THE SWIM The designers' signature leopard print even shows up poolside. The triplex penthouse is perched high above the Milan skyline, with landscaped terraces. The pool is made of volcanic-rock tiles from Stromboli.

For their production this season, the sweeping chords of Pietro Mascagni’s Cavalleria Rusticana (“sweet and strong and romantic”) opened the show, as they have done for thirteen years, only to segue symbolically into poundingly high-voltage disco. In the designers’ new aerie, centuries also collide, and gilded eighteenth- and nineteenth-century furnishings sit comfortably beneath Basquiats and Warhols.
points: In a Milan triplex, Stefano Gabbana and Domenico Dolce have created an environment as glamorous—and leopard-laden—as their fashion.

articles.title: Perfect Fit: Kim Kardashian Celebrates Skims’s First International Flagship in London
articles.summary: London came calling, and Central Cee, Troye Sivan, and Kim Petras joined in on the fun amid fashion week.
body: Body-ody-ody had been the sentiment of London Fashion Week, with designers playing with all things sexy on the runways. And on Friday night, the city got to take that further and indulge in the Skims treatment, as co-founders Kim Kardashian and Jens Grede welcomed friends of the brand to its newly opened Regent Street flagship —the first international standalone store for the shapewear and intimates behemoth.

It was Kardashian’s first time visiting the London store, following its soft opening in July. Naturally, she dressed for the occasion. She wore Ludovic de Saint Sernin’s Mermaid Bi Dress in flesh-toned leather, which closely contoured her curves with a grommet-studded bodice and lace-up slit revealing a sheer underlay beneath. The choice was particularly apt: Kardashian’s forthcoming collaboration with the designer is set to launch October 1, marrying Skims’s shapewear foundations with Saint Sernin’s unapologetically sexy, party-ready signatures. Later, she shimmied into a sculpted chocolate brown corset with belted and tie-up detailing and a hip-skimming maxi skirt.
points: London came calling, and Central Cee, Troye Sivan, and Kim Petras joined in on the fun amid fashion week.

articles.title: Hailey Bieber Debuts Her Darkest Hair Shade in Years
articles.summary: Fall is basically here, and with it, a major seasonal switch-up for Hailey Bieber.
body: In summer, Hailey Bieber shared that she had been on a “ hair health journey. ” She was leaning into her natural light brunette, letting her lengths grow, and generally resisting the urge to make any dramatic moves. Just in time for fall, though, the Rhode beauty mogul seems to have decided her hair can handle a seasonal transformation.

One of Bieber’s go-to hairstylist, Irinel de León (also known for her work with Carey Mulligan and Kendall and Kylie Jenner), shared a look at Bieber’s freshly cut and colored hair, now styled in long, sweeping layers with plenty of dimension and texture around the face. Several inches have been added since she last chopped her hair into the trending clavi-cut, with extension expert Priscilla Valles lending some extra length and fullness. The result is flippy and three-dimensional, with enough movement to keep the darker shade from feeling heavy.
points: Fall is basically here, and with it, a major seasonal switch-up for Hailey Bieber.
